request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIRS:
PAIR 1:
A: perform_retrieve synchronously runs the entire feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) inside the per-URL RetrieveTopic job, duplicating the scheduler's responsibility on a user-triggered path. Every embed of a not-yet-imported article re-fetches and re-imports the whole feed inline (open + parse + one topic per item), so the requesting user's article appears only after the full poll finishes, and N users embedding different articles concurrently run N overlapping full polls that race on the same feed items.
B: P2: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) directly, bypassing the job queue and coupling retriever to feed poller internals, side-stepping retry/queueing semantics

A: P2: TopicEmbed.import re-import with unchanged content (content_sha1 no-op branch) is untested, and the update test doesn't assert content_sha1 persistence or that no duplicate TopicEmbed/topic is created (unique index on embed_url makes a duplicate-creation regression a hard 500)
B: The TopicEmbed update test cannot detect if revision loses raw_html cooking: post.cooked =~ /new contents/ would also pass if PostRevisor cooked the new raw through the regular markdown pipeline (the phrase survives markdown), so nothing verifies cook_method is preserved across revision. Also untested: importing identical content triggers no revision (the content_sha1 guard and embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)), and that update doesn't create a duplicate topic/embed (TopicEmbed.count == 1 never asserted).

PAIR 4:
A: The Disqus importer silently loses its --category option and its permalink-post behavior, switching creation to TopicEmbed.import_remote with no migration note for existing callers. Existing automation invoking `thor disqus:import -c "Some Category"` now fails with an unknown-option error, and previously imported Disqus threads (which got a Permalink link post) would now create raw-HTML embed topics instead — a behavioral change to a public CLI surface with no counterpart or deprecation path in this diff.

Operators who re-run a previously working Disqus import get a different artifact than before: network-dependent imports (can hang/fail per URL), raw-HTML posts bypassing the cooking pipeline, and topics created via the embed path — a changed output contract never surfaced as a decision point.
